config.title: deterministic seed replications of the algebraic-spine and frequency-diversity claims, plus pose-DOF / receiver / pose-count / basis ablations
config.whitening_convention: W = None (identity noise): hh.whiten_realify(A,B,None) returns sqrt(2)*[Re; Im] row stacks; raw identity-noise stacks throughout
config.pose_theta_convention: theta = atan2(-p_y,-p_x): body +x axis points toward the origin

partA_scenes.l2_metric: sample vector 2-norm over the N^2 cell-centre values (no h weighting)

gates.kernel_identity_scale: 1e-8 * max(1, ||A_s||_2^2) for the family-2 subspace-distance gate; identity_support additionally requires equal nullities, cross residuals <= 1e-10, and min singular N1^T N2 > 1-1e-6 when the null spaces are non-empty
gates.check_C: >= 2 of 3 directions with rho movement > 1e-4 (family 4 gate)

partB_pose_dof.pose_column_order: [px, py, theta] repeated per pose t

partD_pose_sweep.geometry: Family-1 arc: R=1.6, phi=linspace(-45,45,T) deg, theta=atan2(-py,-px); q=3T

config.randomness_note: seeded numpy default_rng(1001..1005) only for random scenes; dense linear algebra is deterministic
config.claim_scope: finite-grid (N=16) replications and descriptive ablations only; no continuum transfer, no universal monotonicity theorem, no silent conflation of machine-rank boundary events with exact algebraic violations

c1_kernel_identity.note: N1 = eig(K_SLAM) with |eigenvalue| <= tol; N2 = null(P_perp A) from the full SVD.  Empty bases give distance 0 and vacuous min singular.  max_norm_KSL_on_N2 and max_norm_C_on_N1 are the cross residuals reported by family 2; the literal same-space residuals on N1/N2 are recorded as well.

c3_retention.note: rho = retention_spectrum(A_s, I - Z Z^T); prediction = desc(concat(1 - sv(Z^T Q_A)^2, ones(r_A - len))).

frequency_diversity.directions_method: family4.generalized_eigen_directions(A1, P1), P1 = I - Z Z^T for Range(B1); three ascending (most confounded) directions; u = V_A diag(1/s_A) w

literal_generalized_second_argument_diag.exception_message: matmul: Input operand 1 has a mismatch in its core dimension 0, with gufunc signature (n?,k),(k,m?)->(n?,m?) (size 48 is different from 24)

crosscheck_vs_family2_4.replication_note: two_blob row is compared to results/family2_results.json (cases.smooth) and results/family4_results.json (checks.C) read-only.

partC_receiver_ablation.note: r_A itself changes with measurement count: n_rx=1 gives r_A=12 and Range(B_R)=R^12 (A fully B-confounded, retained 0); n_rx=2 gives r_A=24 with Range(B_R) contained in Range(A_s) (retained 6); n_rx>=4 keeps r_A=24 with a transverse intersection (retained 9.41 for n_rx=4 and 9.40 for n_rx=8). The literal monotonicity flags over the mixed-r_A rows are therefore not interpretable as a pure receiver-count effect.

partD_pose_count_ablation.note: q=3T grows with T and r_A stays 24 (A_s has p=24 columns), so retained mass falls monotonically here (15 -> 9.41 -> 6.58) as more pose nuisance columns occupy more of the data space.

partE_basis_ablation.note: B_R_standard is fixed (r_B=18) while r_A = p grows, so retained mass increases with p (0.157 -> 9.41 -> 18.75) partly because more A directions are added outside the fixed B range; confusable mass also increases (11.84 -> 14.59 -> 17.25).
